_comment: Review-only data for /review/ (built only when PUBLIC_REVIEW_ROUTES=1). Measurements are filled from qa/heroes-2026-10-10/ results; nothing here is shown on production pages.

measured.conditions: Phone positions at 390 x 844 after the movement settles (qa/heroes-2026-10-10/first-screen.json). Speed: Lighthouse 12.8.2 mobile preset (simulated slow 4G, 4x CPU), every page from the same local server, 3 interleaved rounds, median shown; a photo-size pass was needed (first pass: up to 3.15 s and 520 KB) and is included. Differences under about 150 ms are noise. Layout shift measured with and without the font loading late (a size-matched fallback font keeps line breaks identical). Accessibility: axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA with motion and with reduced motion: 0 serious or critical on every option.

1.Brand and proof: Logo as the caller avatar; the brand line acted out. Uses three verbatim Google review excerpts as proof
1.Conversion: Strongest on phones: the first thing on screen is a call banner that is itself the call button, then Call, Request and Text photos
1.Phone, first screen: Call ends 525 px, Request 590 px down an 844 px phone screen
1.Mobile speed (median of 3): score 98, largest paint 2.25 s (runs 2252-2256 ms), layout shift 0.003, 392 KB in 10 requests (live home: 2.03 s, 352 KB, 8)

2.Brand and proof: Most "real business" at a glance: his own van, lettering and decal, at dusk
2.Conversion: Very clear, but on phones the photo comes first, so the buttons sit lowest of the five
2.Phone, first screen: Call ends 704 px, Request 769 px down an 844 px phone screen
2.Mobile speed (median of 3): score 98, largest paint 2.25 s (runs 2103-2257 ms), layout shift 0, 400 KB in 9 requests (live home: 2.03 s, 352 KB, 8)

3.Brand and proof: Shows his craft: a finished boiler, tank and copper manifold, marked up like a drawing, with a logo title block
3.Conversion: Buttons high on phones; the photo follows directly below
3.Phone, first screen: Call ends 440 px, Request 505 px down an 844 px phone screen
3.Mobile speed (median of 3): score 98, largest paint 2.40 s (runs 2335-2402 ms), layout shift 0.003, 417 KB in 10 requests (live home: 2.03 s, 352 KB, 8)

4.Brand and proof: Proof of a whole job, rough stage to finished room, and the only interactive option (drag or arrow keys)
4.Conversion: Buttons high on phones; the compare frame follows directly below. Heaviest of the five (two photos)
4.Phone, first screen: Call ends 440 px, Request 505 px down an 844 px phone screen
4.Mobile speed (median of 3): score 98, largest paint 2.40 s (runs 2342-2553 ms), layout shift 0, 449 KB in 11 requests (live home: 2.03 s, 352 KB, 8)

5.Brand and proof: Most personal: who picks up, his logo, his 14 towns flipping to 24/7. Uses the portrait he dislikes
5.Conversion: Portrait first on phones, so the Request button sits near the bottom of the first screen
5.Phone, first screen: Call ends 735 px, Request 800 px down an 844 px phone screen
5.Mobile speed (median of 3): score 98, largest paint 2.25 s (runs 2253-2258 ms), layout shift 0, 390 KB in 10 requests (live home: 2.03 s, 352 KB, 8)

why: It is the one built around the action you want: on a phone the first thing a visitor sees is a call banner that calls Shane, followed by Call, Request and Text photos, with three customers saying in their own words that he answers and shows up.
It works without a new photo and without the portrait, and it is as fast as the live page within noise (2.25 s largest paint, 392 KB).

If you want the strongest "this is a real local business" picture, option 2 (the van at dusk) is the runner-up; its buttons sit lower on phones. Option 4 is the best proof of craft if you would rather lead with a finished job.
Combining is possible, as with Paci: for example option 2's van on desktop with option 1's call banner on phones.

options.name: Incoming call
options.story: The page opens on the promise: a phone rings, Shane picks up, and three customers' own words arrive as texts (verbatim from his Google reviews). On a phone the first thing you see is a call banner that is itself the call button.
options.motion: Rings and pulses (0-1.6 s), the call connects and the voice line moves, then the three texts arrive (to about 3 s). Then still. With reduced motion: the answered call, straight away.
options.caveat: The phone is an illustration of a call screen, not a screenshot of a real call.

options.name: Blue hour
options.story: Shane's own van photo at dusk, full-bleed: his lettering, his decal, his number. The headline sits on the dark sky; the van is the proof that a real person with a real truck is on the other end.
options.motion: The photo settles from a slight zoom and one pass of evening light crosses it (1.8 s). Then still.
options.caveat: The van lettering in the photo includes Furnaces, which the site does not list yet (owner question S5).

options.name: Mechanical room
options.story: One of his cleanest finished jobs (boiler, storage tank and copper zone manifold) as a marked-up drawing sheet: a scan line passes, callouts name what you are looking at, and the title block carries his logo.
options.motion: Scan line (1.1 s), then three callouts draw in one after another (to about 2 s). Then still.

options.name: Rough to finished
options.story: Two photos from the same job, the rough stage and the finished kitchen, in one frame. The divider sweeps once, then the visitor can drag it (or use the arrow keys) to compare. Proof of the whole job, not just the fixture.
options.motion: One sweep of the divider (0.5-2.4 s), then it waits for the visitor. Without JavaScript or with reduced motion it rests half and half.

options.name: Owner poster
options.story: Shane's portrait as a red-and-charcoal print with his logo badge, and a split-flap board that flips once through his 14 confirmed towns and lands on 24/7. The most personal option: you see who picks up.
options.motion: The print develops (1.3 s) while the board flips through the towns (0.5-2.9 s). Then still.
options.caveat: Uses the portrait Shane has said he does not like. It is included because you allowed keeping his image; a new photo would drop straight into the same treatment.
